metadata.title: COSU Emergency / Safety Console SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan defining Corporate-Owned Single-Use (COSU) Emergency and Safety Consoles as life-safety–critical endpoint execution environments for emergency response and coordination.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: A corporate-owned, single-use endpoint dedicated to emergency notification, safety monitoring, and response coordination during critical incidents, with extreme availability and integrity requirements.

props.name: inherits-from-sspp
props.remarks: COSU Emergency and Safety Consoles inherit foundational endpoint trust governance from the Secure Endpoint Platform SSPP.

props.name: endpoint-class
props.remarks: Single-use COSU endpoint for life-safety and emergency response operations.

props.name: execution-model
props.remarks: Execution is restricted to approved emergency notification, incident management, and safety coordination applications.

props.name: user-authentication-model
props.remarks: Authorized emergency operators authenticate by role; authentication mechanisms must favor availability and rapid access.

props.name: ownership-model
props.remarks: Emergency / Safety Consoles are owned and controlled by the institution.

props.name: management-model
props.remarks: Consoles are centrally managed and support documented emergency operation modes for continuity.

props.name: cryptographic-identity
props.remarks: Device identity is used to establish trust with emergency platforms, alerting systems, and coordination services.

props.name: baseline-hardening
props.remarks: Operating system configuration disables non-essential functionality while preserving emergency usability.

props.name: privilege-boundary
props.remarks: Emergency / Safety Consoles must not support IT system administration, configuration management, or forensic extraction.

props.name: network-access-model
props.remarks: Network access is restricted to emergency notification systems, safety platforms, coordination services, and management endpoints.

props.name: data-persistence
props.remarks: Local persistence is limited to transient incident state and encrypted operational logs required for continuity and review.

props.name: eligible-data-classifications
props.remarks: Emergency Consoles may interact with limited operational and safety data but not sensitive investigative or administrative datasets.

props.name: non-equivalence-statement
props.remarks: Emergency response authority does not imply eligibility for IT administration, security system configuration, or broader endpoint trust.

props.name: availability-requirement
props.remarks: Emergency / Safety Consoles must prioritize uninterrupted operation, fault tolerance, and rapid recovery under crisis conditions.

props.name: monitoring-and-integrity-signals
props.remarks: Console health, reachability, integrity, and alert delivery status are continuously monitored with immediate escalation.

props.name: lifecycle-governance
props.remarks: Provisioning, testing, reset, and retirement of Emergency / Safety Consoles are auditable and subject to change control.

system-implementation.remarks: COSU Emergency and Safety Consoles implement Secure Endpoint patterns with emphasis on life-safety availability, integrity of alerts, and strict privilege separation.

roles.title: Emergency Operations
roles.remarks: Responsible for emergency response coordination and use of Safety Consoles during incidents.

roles.title: Emergency Management Governance
roles.remarks: Defines emergency workflows, escalation procedures, and system scope.

roles.title: Endpoint Security Operations
roles.remarks: Ensures continuous security posture, monitoring, and lifecycle governance of Emergency Consoles.

control-implementation.remarks: Emergency / Safety Console implementations may use hardened workstations or dedicated appliances and are maintained as mission-critical, tightly controlled configuration baselines.
